summary.headline: Balaji Amines Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% YoY to INR403 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25% versus 19% a year earlier.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR403 crore (up about 12% YoY) and EBITDA was INR102 crore against INR68 crore, lifting margin to 25% from 19% in Q4 FY25 and 18% in Q3 FY26. PAT reached INR65 crore versus INR40 crore a year earlier. Management said production was briefly hit in March 2026 by a geopolitical situation but was managed through inventory planning. For FY27 management guided to 10-15% consolidated volume growth in Q&A, and to 20-30% volume growth and 22-23% EBITDA margin by end-FY27 (wording varied during the call). Specialty subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals was running partially during modifications, which depressed its quarterly margins.

segments.name: Amines
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 7,746 MT. Management said DMF and butylamines run at low utilisation as battery-chemical demand has yet to ramp.

segments.name: Amines derivatives
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 8,935 MT; described as a stable operating base.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 10,660 MT. Subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals ran only about 10-20 days a month during modifications, and management said Q4 subsidiary margins are not a usable benchmark.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume growth of 10-15% (Q&A, for this year), with 20-30% volume growth cited for the period to end-FY27 once new plants ramp.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustainable at 22-23% of sales (stated for end-FY27).
Management targets INR3,000 crore revenue in FY28 (said to be reached in 2028); an earlier-cited INR2,000 crore target was referenced by an analyst.
DME plant at Unit 4 expected to commission in Q1 FY27; utilisation of 30-40% in FY27, 50-60% by year-end, and 80-90% in the following year, subject to road transport permission.
Balaji Specialty Chemicals Unit-I (EDA-based DETA, TETA, PIP, AEEA, AEP) expected in H1 FY27; Unit-II Chincholi (HCN, NaCN, EDTA, EDTA-2Na) expected in Q4 FY27.

Standalone capex remaining for DME, NMM and ACN is about INR20 crore; subsidiary capex about INR275-290 crore consolidated this year (INR200-250 crore subsidiary spend). Phase 1 of the INR750 crore expansion is INR350-400 crore.
capex_capacity: Standalone capacity cited by an analyst at 2,93,000 MT; an analyst estimated utilisation at 35-40%, which management did not dispute.
NMM project of 5,000 TPA under execution, commissioning during FY27; improved-process Acetonitrile (ACN) plant to commission in Q2 FY27.
DME plant at Unit 4 (about 1 lakh tonne capacity) ready to commission; road transport permission awaited, expected in about a month per management.
Balaji Specialty Chemicals expansion of about INR750 crore in phases, Maharashtra Mega Project status under Package Scheme of Incentives 2019.
Battery chemicals unit is running at 20-25% capacity, with production also going to agro and pharma uses.
demand_pricing: Management said raw material costs were up to 2-3x normal in some cases; monoethanolamine was cited at about 3x normal.
EDA/DETA prices averaged about INR300/kg in Q4 and were INR270-280 currently, per management.
Indicative prices: DME about INR100-120/kg, ACN about INR240, NMM about INR250-300.
A large metformin customer that backward-integrated still buys DMA-HCl; management put it at 15-20% of outflow for that product.
Ammonia and methanol available; prices volatile, with purchases now made in shorter lots every 3-4 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand with standalone utilisation around 35-40%, and which products are low-utilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new projects are new products, not capacity adds for existing lines. Low utilisation is in DMF, butylamines and battery chemicals (DMC) because battery demand has not started.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken in Q4 and what realisation growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers accepted price increases in Q4 and margins were held through inventory management. Guidance: 20-30% volume growth and 22-23% EBITDA margin by end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR2,000 crore to INR3,000 crore FY28 target realistic given DME approvals and slow specialty demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DME manufacturing permissions are in place and only transport approval is pending. It reaffirmed INR3,000 crore revenue in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary other expenses drop and what are subsidiary raw material trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary worked about 10-15 days a month during modifications, with repair costs partly capitalised. Monoethanolamine costs were about 3x normal. Management said the quarter was not a benchmark and asked analysts to email the company secretary for modelling inputs.

qa_highlights.question: What is remaining standalone capex and FY27 subsidiary capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone balance is about INR20 crore. Subsidiary spend is about INR200-250 crore this year after INR110 crore already spent, for total consolidated capex of INR275-290 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will DME be sold before transport permission arrives and what volume is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Samples went out in 500 kg cylinders for trials, and bulk orders follow permission. Management said FY27 utilisation would be marginal, with 60-70% growth next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company increase its stake in BSE, and what is the status of the greenfield project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake increase needs both boards and shareholders, and an IPO is not yet decided. On capex, it said modifications at the subsidiary began last year, and it plans to invite investors to a plant visit around June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of antidumping duties on DMF and EDA?
qa_highlights.answer: No DMF application has been filed, and the old case remains. The EDA case was at final stage, but duty exemptions run to end-June, so the outcome is pending.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: ammonia, methanol and monoethanolamine prices and supply are moving every few days, and management said margin holds depend on this.
Battery chemicals demand (DMC, DMF, electrolytes) has not ramped, and a plant running at 20-25% is still dependent on a customer start.
DME commissioning depends on road transport permission and the first-time product market acceptance; management guides to 30-40% FY27 utilisation.
Subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals is partly idle during modifications, so its quarterly numbers are not clean; watch Q1 and Q2 FY27 ramp-up.
Antidumping duty decisions on EDA and DMF are pending; government exemptions run to end-June 2026.
Management guidance was inconsistent on FY27 volume growth (10-15% vs 20-30%) and on the FY28 revenue target (INR2,000 crore vs INR3,000 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the expansion pipeline, but vague and inconsistent on numbers: it gave a 10-15% FY27 volume range in one answer and 20-30% in another, and declined to give price-hike quantum or DME revenue timing. Tone turned defensive when analysts questioned the INR3,000 crore FY28 target and subsidiary performance.
key_quotes: Our consolidated EBITDA for Q4 FY26 stood at INR102 crores as compared to INR68 crores in Q4 FY25.
We will be definitely reaching INR3,000 crores in 2028.
Consolidated debt stood at INR133 crores, mainly on account of ongoing expansion related activities.
